previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism was admitted after developing left-sided chest pain, shortness of breath, and bilateral hand cramping immediately following a dialysis session. Initial concerns included air embolism and acute coronary syndrome, but serial cardiac enzymes and EKGs were negative, and chest imaging showed resolution of prior pulmonary edema without new acute findings. Symptoms resolved within hours, and he remained stable on telemetry with controlled heart rate on diltiazem. Potassium levels fluctuated but were managed medically. Cocaine use was noted as a complicating factor, contraindicating beta-blocker use. He was discharged home with instructions to continue dialysis on his regular schedule, monitor for recurrent chest pain, and follow up with cardiology, nephrology, endocrinology, and primary care. Medication adjustments included switching to 90 mg daily cinacalcet and 81 mg chewable aspirin, with continued home therapies for heart failure, diabetes, and hyperthyroidism.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ with DM2, HTN, HLD, ESRD on HD presenting with 
shortness of breath and chest pain after missing HD and meds for 
4 days, found to be overloaded on exam and in atrial 
fibrillation with RVR.

ACTIVE PROBLEMS:
1. HYPOXEMIA secondary to ACUTE PULMONARY EDEMA:  He presented 
with dyspnea and a ___ liter oxygen requirement via nasal 
cannula. Though his CXR revealed little pulmonary edema, though 
he had posterior crackles.  He likely became volume overloaded 
upon missing an HD session over the weekend, which was 
undoubtedly compounded by his atrial fibrillation in RVR.  After 
three dialysis sessions and 4+ liters of fluid removed, his 
oxygen requirement dissipated and his symptoms improved. 

2. ATRIAL FIBRILLATION WITH RVR:  He presented to the ED with a 
HR to 160-175 in atrial fibrillation, which was caused by a 
combination of crack-cocaine abuse, failure to take his 
diltiazem for several days, and volume overload from missed 
dialysis. He was controlled with IV diltiazem and metoprolol in 
the ED.  He began PO diltiazem 90mg QID on the floor with decent 
control, though he did trigger once for tachycardia that was 
responsive to increased diltiazem dose.  He was discharged on 
his home dose of 180mg dilt CR BID. ASA continued for stroke 
PPX- he qualifies for warfarin based on elevated CHADS2 score 
though had significant GI bleeds in the past.  Digoxin also 
continued.

3. ESRD on HD:  He was dialyzed via a left tunneled IJ catheter 
three times.  Epogen was held due to reasonable hemoglobin.  
Sensipar was continued, though PTH noted to be elevated near 
1500.  

4. N/V/D: likely had viral gastroenteritis over the weekend 
prior to admission.

5. CHEST PAIN:  He presented with substernal chest pain that was 
constant in nature over the preceding several days. It improved 
with rate control and dialysis- it may have been demand ischemia 
from tachycardia and crack abuse.  EKG showed no acute ischemic 
changes.

6. DRUG ABUSE:  brief counselling offered

7.  SUICIDAL IDEATION: patient made suicidal comments in the ED 
that he would ""shoot himself in the head"" though later retracted 
them, clearly stating that he has no intention to hurt himself 
and that he was simply upset about being sick.

INACTIVE ISSUES:
8. DM2: continued lantus with HISS per home doses

9. TOBACCO ABUSE: nicotine patch and counselling offered

PENDING TESTS AT DISCHARGE: none

- recent revision of left AV fistula, will f/u with his 
nephrologist re: reinitiating its use.

radiology_notes.text:
PORTABLE CHEST: ___

HISTORY:  ___ male with tachycardia and chest pain.

FINDINGS:  Single portable view of the chest is compared to previous exam from
___.  

Dual-lumen central venous catheter again seen with distal tip within the
proximal right atrium.  There is engorgement of the central pulmonary vascular
markings, and slightly indistinct vascular markings peripherally.  Right-sided
pleural effusion is identified.  Cardiac silhouette is stable as are the
osseous and soft tissue structures.

IMPRESSION:  Engorged pulmonary vasculature and right pleural effusion without
frank pulmonary edema.

INDICATION:  Chest pain, shortness of breath, and AFib with RVR.  Has new
lower extremity pain, worse on the right than the left.

COMPARISON:  Lower extremity Doppler examination, ___.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of lower extremity deep vein thrombosis in the
right or the left leg.  The bilateral common femoral veins have appropriate
flow and appropriate augmentation to Valsalva.  The bilateral common femoral
veins, superficial femoral veins, popliteal veins, posterior tibial veins, and
peroneal veins are compressible with normal flow.  There is no evidence of
thrombus.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of lower extremity DVT.
